methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $60M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
REGENT Craft is a Series A-stage transportation company founded by Billy Thalheimer and Mike Klinker that has raised $60M to date. The transportation sector contains six private peers of varying maturity (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, FleetZero, and Beyond Aero) and no direct public comparables.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method due to data constraints. The Stage-Progression approach uses the $60M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage step-ups, yielding $120M. The Peer-Median method is not applicable here: while three transportation peers exist in the broader dataset, none satisfy the narrow filters required for meaningful comparison (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier). Relying on an all-sector median would introduce excessive noise given the heterogeneity of the transportation peer set.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $102M to $138M, with a median point of $120M. This range reflects both the stage-progression baseline and reasonable variance bounds. Key uncertainties center on the absence of tight-stage comparables—the lack of Series A-stage transportation firms limits calibration of typical step-up multiples and prevents peer-based validation. Resolution of stage-specific metrics and closer identification of same-stage peers would materially improve precision.
